title: Week 1: Introduction to Data Science
text:
Know what data science is and why it is important in the modern world.
Be able to give an example of a data science workflow to follow when working as a data scientist.
Be able to give examples of some tools we can use for Data Science, and discuss the importance of reproducibility.

title: Week 1: Introduction to Data Science
text:
Tools for Data Science

You can do data science in any language.
Some languages are “better” than others:

Community support
Library ecosystem
Performance
Ease of learning
Integration
Reproducibility

title: Week 1: Introduction to Data Science
text:
Most Prominent Languages

Python
R
SQL
Julia
Scala

title: Week 1: Introduction to Data Science
text:
Why R?

Designed specifically for statistics and data analysis
Ecosystem of packages for data manipulation, visualization, and modeling
Support for reproducible research (RMarkdown, Quarto)
Strong community and extensive documentation
Seamless integration with other tools and languages
Free and open source

title: Week 1: Introduction to Data Science
text:
Be Agile






TipNo Best Language



Every language has strengths and weaknesses. Try out more languages, experiment and find what works for you. Switching between languages within a project may be more effective than sticking to one!

text:
This is a double-badged module: MATH2051 and MATH6195. Taught material:

1 hour lecture (16:00-17:00 in 58/1007, L/R C)
2 hour lab (Mondays, 14:00-16:00 in 25/1009)





1 hour session.
I will demo some new techniques that we will focus on in the labs.





2 hour session.
You will code!
Part of the Course Material.

You will be assessed on material from the labs.
I will attempt to record the labs, but cannot guarantee the quality of the recordings.

Both lab worksheets and solutions will still be available to everyone.





Mondays at 13:00 (right before the lab)
In my office (Building 39, Room 2025) or online (link in Teams).





This year I will (initially) attempt to live-stream all lectures and make office hours hybrid.
The objective is to provide another way to engage, using chat, as well as to streamline lecture capture.
Please still come to the lectures. I do not want to lecture to an empty room!





Four take-home mini courseworks. (5% each, total 20%)

Weeks 2, 4, 6 and 10.
You will have one week to complete each coursework.
Submission via GitHub.
Autograded.






Two in-person supervised courseworks. (40% each, total 80%)

A1 Week 8 - Tuesday 10th November, 11:00-13:00, 25/1009. Covers Chapters 1-6.
A2 Week 12 - Tuesday, 8th December, 11:00-13:00, 25/1009. Covers the entire module.






GenAI allowed in take-home, blocked in supervised coursework.
Supervised coursework uses University computers.
You will not be able to complete the assessments if you do not know how to use:

Git (take-home only)
Quarto Notebooks in R.

These are covered in Chapters 2-3 and in every lab.





“R for Data Science”, https://r4ds.hadley.nz
